records.titleEn: General policy structure for positive-lead-time lost-sales inventory
records.inventoryObject: Periodic-review lost-sales inventory with positive lead times; the state includes on-hand and pipeline inventory.
records.decision: Replenishment timing and order quantity, with source selection when supply options are endogenous.
records.uncertainty: Stochastic demand; extensions may include random supply and stochastic delivery times.
records.question: Under general demand, positive lead times, and finite parameters, characterize a computationally tractable optimal policy or establish a uniform nonasymptotic guarantee relative to the globally optimal policy. Delineate when base-stock, constant-order, projected-inventory, or richer state-dependent policies are required.
records.sourceTitle: Learning to Order for Inventory Systems with Lost Sales and Uncertain Supplies
records.sourceEvidence: The anchor paper treats the system as computationally difficult even when the demand and supply distributions are known, and therefore develops efficient learning methods against structured policy benchmarks.
records.knownProgress: Regret guarantees are available for selected lead-time regimes and structured benchmarks. Constant-order, base-stock, and projected-inventory policies are supported under special assumptions or asymptotic regimes.
records.currentAssessment: This is an important but broad structural gap, not a single conjecture stated by one source. A formal release requires a fixed model, benchmark, and performance criterion.
records.nextVerificationAction: Fix the demand and supply assumptions and the finite-horizon or average-cost criterion; audit 2024-2026 work and forward citations on positive-lead-time lost-sales systems.

records.titleEn: Regret to the true optimal policy for arbitrary lead time under uncertain supply
records.inventoryObject: A positive-lead-time lost-sales system with unknown demand and random supply.
records.decision: Sequential online orders, potentially while learning both demand and supply mechanisms.
records.uncertainty: Demand distribution, supply realizations or yields, and censored sales feedback.
records.question: For arbitrary lead times, obtain sublinear regret relative to the globally optimal dynamic policy, or prove an information-theoretic lower bound that explains the lead-time or identifiability restrictions in current results.
records.sourceTitle: Learning to Order for Inventory Systems with Lost Sales and Uncertain Supplies
records.sourceEvidence: The benchmark and lead-time restrictions in the anchor paper leave a natural question about when the globally optimal policy is learnable; the paper does not necessarily state this extension as a formal open problem.
records.knownProgress: Existing algorithms attain regret guarantees against an optimal policy in selected lead-time regimes; more general settings often revert to structured benchmarks such as constant-order policies.
records.currentAssessment: This formulation is an editorial synthesis. The record must be checked against impossibility results and subsequent work that may have removed the lead-time restriction.
records.nextVerificationAction: Audit forward citations and lower bounds; separate censored demand, random yield, and unknown-transition information structures.

records.titleEn: Finite-system guarantees with stochastic lead times and order crossing
records.inventoryObject: Inventory with stochastic lead times, possible order crossing, and indivisible units.
records.decision: Order quantities and pipeline-inventory control.
records.uncertainty: Demand and stochastic lead times, including uncertainty in the arrival order.
records.question: Construct implementable policies with finite-system error bounds for indivisible products and order crossing, without relying on a many-unit scaling limit.
records.sourceTitle: Asymptotic Optimality of Semi-Open-Loop Policies in Inventory Models with Stochastic Lead Times
records.sourceEvidence: The anchor paper develops semi-open-loop policies and proves asymptotic optimality, which leaves finite-system, discrete-unit, and general order-crossing guarantees as natural extensions.
records.knownProgress: Fluid, diffusion, and other large-scale asymptotic results are available; uniform finite-system guarantees remain comparatively limited.
records.currentAssessment: This is an editorially synthesized candidate. The exact model, scaling regime, and post-2026 extensions still require verification.
records.nextVerificationAction: Verify the version of record and search stochastic lead times, order crossing, and finite-system bounds in combination.

records.titleEn: Nonasymptotic control of perishable inventory with positive lead times
records.inventoryObject: Age-structured perishable inventory with lost sales and positive replenishment lead times.
records.decision: Ordering, age-based issuance, and disposal or scrapping.
records.uncertainty: Demand, lifetime, and lead time, with possible random supply.
records.question: Under general issuing rules and finite parameters, derive policy structure, tractable approximations, or nonasymptotic optimality gaps that do not rely solely on high-shortage-cost or large-system asymptotics.
records.sourceTitle: Managing Perishable Inventory Systems with Positive Lead Times: Inventory Position vs. Projected Inventory Level
records.sourceEvidence: The anchor paper emphasizes the high-dimensional and computationally difficult replenishment problem created by positive lead times and compares inventory-position and projected-inventory-level policies.
records.knownProgress: Simple policies are asymptotically optimal in selected cost and scale regimes, and worst-case approximations exist for some capacitated perishable systems.
records.currentAssessment: The source supports a broad research challenge rather than a unique mathematical statement. The record should ultimately separate policy structure, finite-system bounds, and issuing rules.
records.nextVerificationAction: Extract the conclusion and future-work passages; audit general issuing rules, positive lead times, and finite-gap results.

records.titleEn: Tight approximation with capacity, setup costs, and perishability
records.inventoryObject: Age-structured perishable inventory with capacity constraints and fixed ordering costs.
records.decision: Batch size, replenishment timing, issuance, and disposal.
records.uncertainty: Demand and aging, potentially with positive lead times.
records.question: When capacity, setup costs, positive lead times, and perishability coexist, design scalable policies with tight uniform approximation ratios or additive optimality gaps.
records.sourceTitle: Approximation Algorithms for Capacitated Perishable Inventory Systems with Positive Lead Times
records.sourceEvidence: The anchor paper establishes approximation algorithms and worst-case guarantees for capacitated perishable inventory; tighter guarantees under richer cost and lead-time structures are natural extensions.
records.knownProgress: Approximation guarantees are known for selected capacitated perishable models, including balancing and truncated-balancing policies.
records.currentAssessment: This is an editorial synthesis. A more general model should not be labeled a recognized open problem without direct source support and a current-status audit.
records.nextVerificationAction: Audit the intersection of fixed ordering costs, positive lead times, and perishability, with particular attention to constant-factor guarantees.
records.notes: Related: Zhang, Ayer, and White (2023), https://doi.org/10.1287/msom.2022.0644

records.titleEn: Exact optimal policy structure for general dual sourcing
records.inventoryObject: A dual-sourcing system with regular and expedited suppliers that differ in cost and lead time.
records.decision: Order quantities by source, inventory targets, and expediting triggers.
records.uncertainty: Stochastic demand, with possible supply risk and lead-time uncertainty.
records.question: Under general demand, cost, and lead-time primitives, characterize the exact optimal policy or obtain a uniform finite-system guarantee for a simple policy relative to the globally optimal policy.
records.sourceTitle: Control of Dual-Sourcing Inventory Systems Using Recurrent Neural Networks
records.sourceEvidence: The anchor paper motivates a recurrent-neural-network policy by the computational difficulty of solving a general dual-sourcing inventory model exactly.
records.knownProgress: Dual-index, tailored base-surge, critical-set base-surge, distributionally robust, and neural policies are supported under special structures or asymptotic regimes.
records.currentAssessment: This is a longstanding research challenge. It should be partitioned by single-item versus assembly structure, deterministic versus stochastic lead times, and known versus unknown distributions.
records.nextVerificationAction: Build a result matrix recording model assumptions, policy class, exact versus asymptotic guarantee, and whether the guarantee is finite-system.

records.titleEn: Dual sourcing in assembly systems beyond current asymptotic regimes
records.inventoryObject: A multi-component assembly system in which each component can be obtained from regular and expedited sources.

records.sourceTitle: Dual Sourcing in an Assembly System: A Simple and Effective Critical-Set Base-Surge Policy
records.sourceEvidence: The anchor paper develops a critical-set base-surge policy with strong performance in specified regimes, exposing the absence of general finite-system guarantees.
records.knownProgress: Critical-set structure and asymptotic performance guarantees are available in selected regimes.
records.currentAssessment: The source supports a clear research challenge. A public statement must list the existing theorem conditions so that covered regimes are not relabeled as open.
records.nextVerificationAction: Extract every theorem assumption and asymptotic regime, then audit subsequent work on dual sourcing in assembly systems.

records.titleEn: Optimal policy for one-warehouse multi-retailer systems without the balance assumption
records.inventoryObject: A one-warehouse, multi-retailer inventory system, potentially with perishable items or feature-informed demand.
records.decision: Warehouse replenishment, retailer allocation, and retailer inventory control.
records.uncertainty: Retailer demand, covariates, and common shocks, potentially with censoring.

records.knownProgress: Taylor-approximation policies have asymptotic guarantees under many-retailer scaling; data-driven variants establish consistency or sample-performance results.
records.currentAssessment: This is suitable for the formal-candidate track, but the dated open-status assessment remains provisional pending page-level source storage and independent expert review.
records.nextVerificationAction: Store the exact source passage and page; audit author follow-up work, forward citations, and exact results that avoid the balance assumption.
auditFlags: Normalize the bibliographic year: the article was published online in 2024 and appears in Management Science volume 71(1) in 2025.
Store the exact no-balance-assumption passage and page before public Type A release.

records.titleEn: Exact finite-horizon control for multiwarehouse-multistore lost-sales systems with fixed costs
records.inventoryObject: A multiwarehouse, multistore lost-sales system with fixed ordering or shipment costs.
records.decision: Warehouse and store replenishment, batching, and allocation.

records.question: Characterize exact finite-horizon or average-cost control, or obtain a uniform performance bound that does not require a long planning horizon.

records.nextVerificationAction: Verify the horizon and parameter dependence in the existing bounds; audit exact structure and lower bounds for multiechelon lost-sales models with fixed costs.

records.titleEn: Exact optimal policy for two-echelon stochastic distribution systems with fixed shipment costs
records.inventoryObject: A two-echelon stochastic distribution system with fixed shipment costs.

records.question: Characterize the exact optimal policy or identify a computationally equivalent low-dimensional structure under general conditions.

records.titleEn: Optimal joint inventory and pricing control for a one-warehouse multistore system
records.inventoryObject: A one-warehouse, multistore inventory network with price-responsive demand.

records.titleEn: Dynamic regret for network inventory under unknown nonstationarity and prediction quality

records.titleEn: Multistage decision-focused inventory learning at network scale
records.inventoryObject: A multistage, multi-SKU, or multinode inventory network.

records.titleEn: Unified benefit-cost-carbon accounting for AI-enabled inventory systems
records.inventoryObject: Inventory systems that use forecasting, reinforcement learning, generative AI, or autonomous agents.
records.decision: Model selection, deployment, retraining, human supervision, and allocation of computational resources.
records.uncertainty: Model drift, decision error, computing prices, energy use, and emissions.
records.question: Develop a decision-level accounting framework that evaluates inventory cost and service improvements jointly with the life-cycle cost of data, computing, maintenance, supervision, governance, and carbon emissions.
records.sourceTitle: OM Forum-Supply Chain Management in the AI Era: A Vision Statement from the Operations Management Community

records.knownProgress: Model-efficiency metrics, green computing, monitoring systems, and conventional inventory-cost measures provide components, but a unified decision-level framework is not established.
records.currentAssessment: This is a source-backed infrastructure agenda, not a single mathematical conjecture.

records.titleEn: Resolved control: approximation guarantees for inventory staggering
records.inventoryObject: Multiple periodically replenished items whose phases are staggered to smooth a shared capacity or workload.
records.decision: Replenishment phases, group synchronization, and staggering schedules.
records.uncertainty: Demand or cost parameters, cycle lengths, and shared resource load.
records.question: Historical question: can one derive improved approximation and structural guarantees for inventory staggering, including groupwise synchronization and sampling-based construction?
records.sourceTitle: New Approximation Guarantees for the Inventory Staggering Problem
records.sourceEvidence: The anchor paper develops new approximation guarantees and directly establishes sampling-complexity and groupwise-synchronization results that had been treated as candidate gaps in the initial audit.
records.knownProgress: The 2026 paper proves the principal guarantees attached to the original record. Extensions with additional side constraints may remain interesting but constitute different questions.
records.currentAssessment: Reclassified as a resolved control. The earlier formal-candidate label conflated results proved in the anchor paper with genuinely unresolved extensions.
records.nextVerificationAction: Map each historical question to the corresponding theorem and retain only assumption-changing extensions as separate candidate records.

records.titleEn: Resolved control: regret against the optimal base-stock policy in lost-sales systems with lead times
records.inventoryObject: A positive-lead-time lost-sales system in which latent demand is censored by sales.
records.decision: Online ordering and learning of a base-stock level.
records.uncertainty: Unknown demand and censored sales feedback.
records.question: Historical question: can an algorithm attain near-optimal regret relative to the best base-stock policy in a lost-sales system with lead times?
records.sourceTitle: Closing the Gap: A Learning Algorithm for Lost-Sales Inventory Systems with Lead Times
records.sourceEvidence: The source explicitly aims to close this gap and proves learning guarantees relative to the optimal base-stock policy.
records.knownProgress: The anchor paper and subsequent work close the central gap for the base-stock benchmark. Regret relative to the globally optimal dynamic policy is a distinct problem.
records.currentAssessment: This record is retained as a resolved control so that benchmark-specific resolutions are not later presented as active open problems.
records.nextVerificationAction: Map the historical statement, resolution theorem, and later extensions, preserving the distinction between a base-stock and globally optimal benchmark.

records.titleEn: Resolved control: near-optimal dynamic policies for joint replenishment

records.titleEn: Resolved control: removing the logarithmic loss for reusable-resource allocation
records.inventoryObject: Reusable resource units that become unavailable for a stochastic duration and later return to inventory.
records.decision: Online assortment or allocation, admission control, and inventory-feasibility enforcement.
records.uncertainty: Nonstationary arrivals, heterogeneous request rewards, usage durations, and customer choice.
records.question: Historical question: can the competitive guarantee for reusable resources be improved from 1-O(sqrt(log k/k)) to 1-O(1/sqrt(k))?
records.sourceTitle: Technical Note—Near-Optimal Bayesian Online Assortment of Reusable Resources
records.sourceEvidence: Open Problems in OR record W4285091035_p0 extracts the paper's explicit request to remove the logarithmic factor. Aminian, Niazadeh, and Nuti (2026) subsequently obtain 1-sqrt(2/(pi k))+O(1/k) for a Bayesian reusable-resource allocation model and state that this solves the earlier rate question.
records.knownProgress: The 2024 paper obtains 1-O(sqrt(log k/k)). The 2026 working paper matches the leading nonreusable benchmark order for a reusable allocation model.
records.currentAssessment: This is a scope-sensitive resolved control, not an active open problem. The 2026 allocation model must still be mapped carefully to the customer-choice assortment model before claiming resolution of every assortment variant.
records.nextVerificationAction: Complete an assumption-by-assumption mapping between the reusable allocation and assortment models, including choice substitution, arrival processes, rewards, and duration distributions.
records.notes: Cross-registry provenance: Open Problems in OR W4285091035_p0. Candidate resolution: Aminian, Niazadeh, and Nuti (2026), https://ssrn.com/abstract=6384158.
auditFlags: Resolution scope requires expert review before the assortment variant is treated as fully closed.

records.titleEn: Sharp decentralization condition during inventory disruptions
records.inventoryObject: A distribution system with a central warehouse, multiple retailers, expediting, and an upstream disruption mode.
records.decision: Whether disrupted-mode inventory should be centralized at the warehouse or decentralized across retailers.
records.uncertainty: Poisson demand, disruption duration, upstream availability, and expedited fulfillment cost.
records.question: Determine the smallest universal constant epsilon_0 for which the tail comparison underlying the decentralization result holds whenever lambda >= a + epsilon_0. The current proof uses epsilon_0=1, whereas a counterexample implies epsilon_0>0.25.
records.sourceTitle: Managing Multitier Inventory Networks with Expediting Under Normal and Disrupted Modes
records.sourceEvidence: Endnote 3 explicitly asks whether the sufficient requirement lambda >= a+1 can be tightened to lambda >= a+epsilon_0 and records a counterexample showing that any universal epsilon_0 must exceed 0.25.
records.knownProgress: The paper proves the required Poisson-tail comparison for epsilon_0=1 and uses it to obtain a simple decentralization criterion during disruptions.
records.currentAssessment: This is a precise formal candidate from a 2026 UTD journal article. Its operational importance is narrower than the paper's broader inventory-positioning contribution, and current open status still requires a targeted mathematical literature audit.
records.nextVerificationAction: Store the exact endnote and lemma statement, search sharp Poisson-tail comparison results, and seek confirmation from the authors or a probability expert.
records.notes: Exact source location: Section 7, Endnote 3 of the publisher PDF.

records.titleEn: Necessary conditions for four-threshold inventory reset policies
records.inventoryObject: Inventory that must be fully reset periodically and may also be reset early, as in water storage or limited-duration retail product lines.
records.decision: Whether to discard all inventory and, conditional on retaining or resetting the system, how much to order.
records.uncertainty: Demand, contamination or aging cost, shortage cost, and reset cost.
records.question: Characterize weaker or necessary conditions under which the optimal reset-and-order policy retains the four-threshold structure established under the paper's sufficient conditions.
records.sourceAuthors: Lee, Mintz, Aswani, Shen, and Yang (2025)
records.sourceTitle: Optimal Policy for Inventory Management with Periodic and Controlled Resets
records.sourceEvidence: The conclusion states that the sufficient conditions for the threshold structure appear conservative rather than necessary and leaves their relaxation to future research.
records.knownProgress: Under the stated sufficient conditions, the paper proves a four-threshold optimal policy and provides an efficient numerical method.
records.currentAssessment: This is an explicit structural question in a 2025 UTD journal article. A formal release should specify which assumptions are candidate relaxations and what counterexamples are already known.
records.nextVerificationAction: Extract each sufficient condition, test necessity computationally, and audit subsequent work on controlled resets and nonconvex inventory value functions.
records.notes: Exact source location: conclusion of the published paper; the statement is structural rather than a single numerical conjecture.

records.titleEn: Optimal replenishment and issuance under age-sensitive demand and general lifetimes
records.inventoryObject: A finite-horizon perishable-inventory system in which customer utility depends on the remaining lifetime of the issued unit.
records.decision: Joint replenishment and age-based issuance.
records.uncertainty: Demand and the age composition of available inventory.
records.question: For general product lifetimes, characterize the optimal joint replenishment and issuance policy or derive a worst-case performance guarantee for a tractable bucket policy.
records.sourceTitle: Please Customers or Prevent Wastage? Replenishment and Issuance Policy for a Perishable Product with Age-Sensitive Demand
records.sourceEvidence: The paper gives a threshold characterization for a two-period lifetime but reports that optimal issuance can be complex for longer lifetimes; its general-lifetime contribution relies on bucket policies and computational performance.
records.knownProgress: For a two-period lifetime, the optimal issuance rule first uses new units up to a threshold and then follows FIFO. For general lifetimes, the best bucket policy is close to optimal on the reported instances, and the proposed heuristic is asymptotically optimal as unit price grows.
records.currentAssessment: This is a source-backed research challenge rather than a stated conjecture. The absence of a worst-case bound should be verified against subsequent work before the record is promoted.
records.nextVerificationAction: Audit forward citations and general-lifetime perishable issuing models; separate exact policy structure from worst-case approximation guarantees.
records.notes: Publisher abstract and paper scope verified; the open formulation is an editorial synthesis.
